title: CLAUDE.md's version fix lives in the generated region and will be reverted
body:
# 0029: CLAUDE.md's version fix lives in the generated region and will be reverted

## Tags

docs, generated-files, upstream, highlander

## Summary

`CLAUDE.md` was corrected earlier on 2026-08-24 to stop pinning an Intent version in prose -- it had said v2.18.0 while the tool had moved to v2.19.0. That correction was written at line 3, which is **inside the region a regeneration overwrites**, and the current template still interpolates a version there. So the fix is not durable: the next regeneration restores the copied fact, and the file quietly re-acquires the defect it was just cleaned of.

Half of this is devbin's and half is upstream in Intent's templates -- the same split as issue 0004.

## Reproduction

Read the template that generates the file:

```
$ sed -n '3p' /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intentv2/lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md
This project uses Intent v[[INTENT_VERSION]]. The primary config file ...

$ tail -1 /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intentv2/lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md
_Generated from `lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md` for Intent v[[INTENT_VERSION]]._
```

Then locate the preserved region in this project's `CLAUDE.md`: `<!-- user:start -->` at line 52, `<!-- user:end -->` at line 55, and the block between them empty. Line 3's correction is outside it; so is the footer at line 59, which still reads `for Intent v2.18.0` and therefore already contradicts the corrected prose three lines from the top of the same file.

## Root Cause

Two independent facts land in the same file with different lifetimes, and nothing marks which is which:

- **The version is a copied fact.** `intent --version` owns it. Any second copy drifts, which is this project's no-tallies rule; the template makes a fresh copy on every regeneration.
- **A generation stamp and a version pin are indistinguishable in prose.** `for Intent v2.18.0` in the footer is TRUE as provenance -- the file really was generated then, by that version -- and reads as a current-version claim. The reader cannot tell the two apart, so the true statement and the stale one look identical.

The deeper class: **a fix applied to a generated region is not a fix, it is a delay.** Nothing about editing line 3 announced that the edit was perishable, and the file's own marker comment ("Preserved across regeneration") is attached only to the region that *is* preserved -- it says nothing about the far larger region that is not.

## Impact

Low blast radius, indefinite recurrence. `CLAUDE.md` is loaded into context on every Claude Code session in this project, so a stale version claim is read first and questioned last -- the same property that made `.claude/restart.md` the least accurate file in the repository earlier the same day. No code path depends on it.

The upstream half affects **every** Intent project, not just this one: each generated `CLAUDE.md` carries the same interpolated copy.

## Proposed Fix

Devbin's half, done now: state the correction inside `<!-- user:start -->` / `<!-- user:end -->`, which regeneration preserves. That does not stop line 3 reverting; it means a reader who reaches the bottom of the file is told the number above is provenance rather than a pin.

Intent's half, NOT done and not devbin's to do: drop the version interpolation from the template's prose, keeping it only in the footer and marking it explicitly as a generation stamp. Something like `_Generated from ... by Intent vX.Y.Z; `intent --version` owns the current version._ Routed to hv rather than actioned -- this project has no authorisation to edit Intentv2's templates, and Intent runs its own sessions.

## Related

- 0004 -- session-gate docs vs reality; also half upstream in Intent's templates
- `intent/llm/LESSONS.md` -- "Documenting is a test"

## Resolutions

**FIXED 2026-08-25, upstream, and the devbin half turned out not to be the fix.**

hv ruled BOTH TREES, DEVBIN WAITS: land the template fix in v2 and v3, and hold devbin's upgrade until it did, so one apply closed this and 0030 together rather than two. Routed through `intent/vc` to `intent/cc`; devbin edited neither tree.

**The fix.** `lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md:3` no longer interpolates `[[INTENT_VERSION]]` at all, and the footer became `_Generated by Intent v[[INTENT_VERSION]] from ..._`. Committed as Intent `7b723dfa` / Intentv2 `3e7feee3`, both carrying blob `fc34f449` -- byte-identity proven from the committed record, not a worktree compare. Local only; hv accepted knowingly that `v2-maintenance` has no upstream (`rc=128`) so this reaches this machine's fleet and no other.

**The wording was not a new convention, which is what made it cheap to rule on.** `_AGENTS.md` and v3's `views.rs:222` already emit the agentive `Generated by`; `_CLAUDE.md` was the lone holdout. "by" carries provenance where "for" reads as a current-version claim. A longer, more explicit form was proposed from here and withdrawn on Highlander grounds -- two footer conventions in one estate is what the rule forbids.

**The date stays refused, and that is not an oversight.** `b277013a` refused `[[DATE]]` deliberately: a generated file that stamps its own generation differs from itself on every run. Restoring the date was this project's first proposal and would have reversed a ratified call. **And removing the date is what made this defect worse in the first place** -- with the date present the footer read as a record of an event; without it the footer's whole remaining content was a version number, so it read as a pin. Two correct decisions, one seam. The fix repairs the seam in prose instead of reinstating the token.

**THE FIX BROKE A READER OF THE THING IT TOUCHED, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH READING.** `intent_claude_upgrade:50` detected its own output with a CONTIGUOUS string, `Generated from \`lib/templates/llm/_CLAUDE.md\``. The new footer put `by Intent v2.19.0` between the two halves, so the shipped template no longer contained the marker the shipped tool used to recognise its own output. Every project that upgraded would have had its `CLAUDE.md` classified as user-authored thereafter, receiving no further canon change -- **and the tool's own remedy on that branch is `--force`, which skips the preserve step and destroys the `<!-- user:start -->` block.** The remedy was worse than the defect: the original reverted one prose line, this discards the user's own directives.

It failed as a LEGITIMATE MESSAGE. `user-authored (left alone)` is a real, long-standing, correct state, quoted approvingly in this estate's own Laksa and Anvil canary reports. Nothing in the output separates the design from the defect.

Found from devbin by running the upgrade a second time as an idempotency check -- **and misread first**: `0 actions, CLAUDE.md: user-authored` was read as a clean idempotent pass before the predicate was checked. Repaired by `intent/cc` as Intent `2fc66d8f` / Intentv2 `4836d667`, anchoring the mark on the PATH, which recognises the new and historic footers both. **The defect was in the DETECTOR, not in any consumer's file, so every consumer self-healed with no re-apply** -- devbin's `CLAUDE.md` reads `UP TO DATE` again without being touched.

**One claim made from here was refuted.** "A regression test would have failed the moment that commit landed, and no test anyone had would have." One did: `tests/unit/intent_claude_upgrade.bats:86` asserted the literal `Generated from` and went red immediately, in the very file the new test was being asked for. `intent/vc` backed the wrong framing too, having grepped for two identifiers that file does not contain because the test asserts the string's VALUE -- an instrument's silence reported as absence. The durable form is `intent/cc`'s: **this was not an unasserted property, it was a template change committed without running the test file that covers that template. A missing test is a backlog item; an unrun test is a discipline failure, and only one of those is fixed by writing more tests.**

**devbin's own half, which had already landed, was the wrong shape too.** The note inside the preserved block explained that the template interpolates a version into its prose. Once the template stopped doing that, the note was false. It has been rewritten to describe the footer as provenance and to name the commits. A note describing a defect outlives the defect unless something rewrites it.
